name: carousel-cards

frames.best_why: The saved Dolomites card is centred with its rating, dates and price readable.

tagline: Flick a rail of trip cards; it glides, tilts and snaps one card to centre.
summary: A horizontal rail of travel listing cards with drawn landscape covers. The centred card shows its rating, dates and price, hearts save favourites, and the rail snaps between cards with momentum.
appearance: A dark section header pairs a small eyebrow and the heading Weekend escapes with a 02/08 counter and two round arrow buttons. Tall 4:5 cards show flat mountain, dune or lake scenes in greys, each with a small white nights badge, a white heart and a title and location underneath.
behaviour: Dragging or flicking the rail carries momentum and springs to the nearest card, while edges rubber-band. As cards move they tilt in depth, the scene layers parallax and the centre card's rating, dates and price fade in; hearts fill red, arrows and keyboard step one card.
demo_content: Eight trips such as Weekend in Lisbon, Slow days in the Dolomites and Two nights in the dunes, priced in euros.
search_phrases: travel card rail you can flick
cards tilt and zoom toward the centre
use_when: A page should browse a set of destination or product cards without leaving the section.
avoid_when: Browsers without scroll-driven animations lose the tilt and parallax; details only show on the centre card.
customise: Items, title, eyebrow, initial favourites and callbacks are props; the drawn scenes, tilt timing and rail styling live in the file.
weight_why: A hand-rolled momentum spring plus eight cards with scroll-driven depth; idle when not scrolling.

a11y.note: The rail takes arrow, Home and End keys, hearts are labelled buttons, and reduced motion drops tilt and parallax.

issues: Card titles and supporting text are tiny and very dim against the black stage.
Uncentred cards hide rating, dates and price, so they read as unlabelled pictures.
polish_why: Clever momentum rail, but dark scenes and faint off-centre text make it hard to read.
title: Carousel Cards
